label: Wesley A. Watters
narrative: Watters is the Galileo Project's methodological anchor - a planetary scientist and Wellesley astronomy professor who coordinates the project's observatory research and co-edited the Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation special issue that assembled, for the first time, a peer-reviewed corpus on hardware and software specifically designed to detect and characterise unidentified aerospace phenomena. The preface he co-wrote with Richard Cloete, Sarah Little, Avi Loeb and Abraham Lux is the document that establishes there is now a legitimate instrumentation literature in this field rather than a claims literature. His contribution is unglamorous and load-bearing: definitions, sensor calibration, and the discipline of publishing the detection criteria before the detections.
